chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Fadalah, from al-Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the Imams (peace be upon them both), who said:
"If a man divorces his wife with two divorces, then divorces her with the third, while he is ill, then she inherits him."

key_terms.اَلثَّالِثَةَ: The third (divorce, which makes the marriage irrevocable)
key_terms.تَطْلِيقَتَيْنِ: Two divorces (referring to the first two revocable divorces)
key_terms.مَرِيضٌ: Ill/sick (referring to the state of death-illness)

ai.seo_question: Does a wife inherit her husband if he divorces her three times before dying of illness?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies that the third divorce (talqah thalath) does not sever the marital bond for inheritance purposes if the husband dies during the waiting period (iddah) of that specific divorce while ill. This ruling is significant in Shia jurisprudence as it distinguishes between the finality of the divorce for remarriage without a new contract and the immediate right of inheritance, emphasizing that the marital link persists until the iddah concludes. It highlights the principle that death during the iddah of the third divorce treats the wife as a full heir, unlike cases where the divorce might be considered irrevocable (mubarrimah) in other contexts.
